concept.name: Liquidity mining
concept.definition: Liquidity mining is a token incentive program in which a protocol distributes its governance tokens to users who provide liquidity (or other desired behavior), subsidizing early liquidity and decentralizing token ownership.
concept.intuition: It is paying suppliers in company stock to stock the shelves: the protocol rents liquidity with newly minted tokens instead of cash.
concept.mechanics: The protocol allocates an emission budget to targeted pools; LPs stake their LP tokens in a mining contract and accrue pro-rata governance token rewards (e.g. Uniswap's 2020 program paid 5M UNI per pool to ETH/USDT, ETH/USDC, ETH/DAI and ETH/WBTC LPs). Rewards are additive to trading fees and typically decline as programs end or more capital joins.
concept.failure_modes: Mercenary capital arrives for emissions and leaves the moment they stop, so TVL and liquidity evaporate post-program; large emissions dilute the token and create persistent sell pressure ('farm and dump').
concept.misconceptions: Liquidity mining rewards are not protocol revenue or profit-sharing — they are dilutive token issuance paying for growth. A high liquidity-mining APR says nothing about the pool's organic fee economics.
concept.example: Uniswap's September 2020 liquidity mining program distributed 83,333 UNI per pool per day across four v2 pools for two months; participating LPs earned UNI on top of the standard 0.3% swap fees.
